text.p: Iridium LLC said its five satellites had successfully seperated from a Delta II rocket made by McDonnell Douglas Corp, completing the latest deployment to its satellite network.
The separation took place approximately 1-1/2 hours after the satellites were launched from Vandenberg Air Force Base in Lompoc, Calif.
The deloyment brings the total number of Iridium orbiting satellites to 17.
Iridium is building a network of 66 low-earth-orbit satellites to provide telcommunications services on a worldwide basis. The total cost of the project is $4.4 billion.
The company plans to launch all remaining satellites by the summer of 1998 and plans to begin providing telecommuncations services to subscribers by September of 1998.
Iridium is an international consortium of telecommunications and industrial companies. U.S. owners include Motorola Inc, Lockheed Martin Corp and Sprint Corp.
